title.narrative: Papua New Guinea Institutional Partnerships Program

description.narrative: The Papua New Guinea Institutional Partnerships Program (PIPP) is a whole-of-government engagement program involving Australian Government Agencies that provides public service policy, strategic advice and capacity development including administrative leadership and management support to counterpart Papua New Guinea Government agencies. Areas targeted for assistance include: law and justice, security, stability, economic governance, public leadership and policy, and corporate support.

title.narrative: Papua New Guinea Institutional Partnership Program (PIPP) - Independent Mid-Term Review - evaluation report and management response
Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: In 2023 the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) supported PNG’s National Statistics Office (NSO) to develop new systems for Gross Domestic Product (GDP) production. Through targeted training and capacity building the ABS helped PNG collect, compile, and communicate data, resulting in improved GDP reporting timeliness. 2022 GDP figures were released on 2 November 2023, reducing the time lag from the reference year from 22 months to 10 months, in line with IMF recommendations. The shorter timeframe helps enhance the NSO’s credibility and increases the value of this important macroeconomic indicator. It allows the Bank of PNG and PNG Treasury to make timely policy decisions and more accurately monitor government spending and the supply of money in PNG’s economy.

In 2023 the Australian Public Service Commission (APSC) reviewed the PNG Public Service Male Advocacy Network (MAN) Terms of Reference (ToR) and National Public Service Gender Equity and Social Inclusion (GESI) Policy. The MAN’s objective is to train men to support women’s equality, human rights and access to justice and support services. Male public servants volunteer in these roles, responding to and preventing gender-based violence in the workplace. The APSC diversity and inclusion team provided examples of Australian experience and drew on international best practice as part of the review. The MAN ToR were endorsed in April 2023, reinvigorating the network with regular meetings. The APSC also worked with the PNG Department of Personnel Management to support their first International Women’s Day celebrations.

Joint cross-border patrols (JCBPs) in the Torres Strait remain a key cornerstone of the relationship between PNG Customs and the Australian Border Force and Home Affairs. They offer opportunities for joint border enforcement while also collecting information to help inform future enforcement activities on both sides. ‍ JCBPs resumed in 2022 after a pause during the COVID-19 pandemic and continued this reporting period (2023). PNG Customs is the lead PNG agency for the patrols and Australian deployees under the PNG Institutional Partnerships Program (PIPP) supported their work by providing technical guidance that strengthened their ability to deploy. Three patrols were undertaken in 2023 (June and two more between July – December). The patrols presented a unified law enforcement presence in the region.

Papua New Guinea Treasury, with the support from Australian Treasury under the PNG Institutional Partnerships Program, is empowering junior staff to contribute to the delivery of the country’s national budget. Budgets are a key way for governments to allocate resources and communicate priorities, while also facilitating government transparency and accountability. Well-formulated budgets can facilitate economic growth and high-quality government service delivery. Automation of the budget can reduce errors, speed up processes and improve consistency. An uplift in PNG’s budget management improves fiscal transparency – making it easier for international organisations, partner countries and potential investors to assess PNG’s economy and improve engagement. The 2024 Budget process in PNG saw responsibilities distributed amongst all staff, improving internal relationships, while some processes were automated. The inclusion of junior Treasury staff in the process ensured ownership to provide specialised content input, built their skills and awareness, better preparing them for advancement into leadership roles. The budget process is now less dependent on particular individuals, making it more sustainable in the event of staff turnover, while also freeing up Treasury leadership for more strategic engagement.

Papua New Guinea and Australia work together to strengthen the PNG Government's capacity to address transnational crime and promote the rule of law. Money laundering, fraud and drug trafficking are some of the crimes that often involve foreign jurisdictions. PNG faces some issues in prosecuting crimes involving foreign jurisdictions, including money laundering, fraud and drug trafficking. Specific challenges include obtaining critical evidence, tracing proceeds of crime and extraditing accused persons located overseas for criminal investigations and prosecutions. With support from Australia's Attorney-General's Department under the PNG Institutional Partnerships Program, the PNG Department of Justice and Attorney-General (DJAG)’s capacity to prosecute crimes involving foreign jurisdictions has been enhanced. DJAG is on the cusp of approving and operationalising its Central Authority Handbook, detailing specific procedures for DJAG to follow for mutual assistance requests in criminal matters, extradition requests and proceeds of crime. The handbook will also serve as a national resource for law enforcement and legal training.

The Australian Taxation Office and the Papua New Guinea Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) are working in partnership to improve communications and foster voluntary tax compliance. The aim of the project is for the IRC to communicate clearly with all stakeholders so that they understand their tax obligations and the consequences associated with non-compliance. Direct support focused on IRC’s written correspondence has greatly enhanced the effectiveness of communication, ensuring clarity and reducing the risk of misunderstanding across taxpayers with varying literacy levels. Overcoming challenges around lack of capacity in existing IT systems was critical for generating successful outcomes and ensuring sustainability. On 15 May 2024, the IRC Commissioner launched the "New Look Letters for the IRC" at a well-attended ceremony in Port Moresby. Media presence at the event resulted in significant publicity across print, TV and social media. This launch, and the messaging around it, has increased awareness amongst taxpayers and tax agents who can now better understand their obligations, as well as the consequences of non-compliance.
